title: Psychology of Light: How Light Influences the Health and Psyche

findings.consequent: Human perception, psychophysical well-being
findings.mechanism: Light influences human perception and psychophysical well-being.
findings.quote: Light is the stimulus that influences most the human perception, but also the psychophysical well-being of the individual in everyday life.

findings.consequent: Mood
findings.mechanism: Dark and lighting deprivation act as environmental conditioning on mood.
findings.quote: Even the dark and lighting deprivation were considered, not only as environmental conditioning on the mood (Fusco, 2005a)

findings.antecedent: Light (type and range of exposure, colors)
findings.consequent: Perceptual apparatus stimulation, specific emotional states, behavior
findings.mechanism: Light stimulates perceptual apparatus, inducing specific emotional states or behavior.
findings.quote: light may stimulate our perceptual apparatus through type and range of exposure to a lighting source and its colours, inducing specific emotional states or behaviour

findings.antecedent: Strategic layout and modulation of lighting
findings.consequent: Perceiver's mood (calm/rest, mystery/suspense)
findings.mechanism: Strategic layout and modulation of lighting influences the perceiver's mood.
findings.quote: The strategic layout and modulation of lighting by light designers may influence the perceiver's mood, creating a sense of calm and rest

findings.consequent: Specific emotional states (dynamism, relaxation, privacy, visual clarity, excitation, productivity, efficiency, stress, sleepiness, sadness, agitation, restlessness, anxiety), specific cognitive skills
findings.mechanism: Light intensity, saturation, and modulation induce specific emotional states and activate cognitive skills.
findings.quote: light is able to induce—according to its intensity, saturation and modulation—specific emotional states, but also activate specific cognitive skills

findings.antecedent: Variation in light stimuli (bright/dim, uniform/non-uniform, central/perimeter, warm/cool)
findings.consequent: Psychophysiological responses
findings.mechanism: Variations in light stimuli induce changes in psychophysiological responses.
findings.quote: it is possible to induce a change of the psychophysiological responses by the perceiver through the alteration/modulation of the nature and typology of light stimuli

findings.consequent: Range of emotional responses
findings.mechanism: Adding a sound stream to light impact enhances emotional responses.
findings.quote: the range of emotional responses by each individual exposed to the light, grow if besides the impact generated by a light source—we also add a sound stream

findings.consequent: Tactile sensation (perceived temperature)
findings.mechanism: Colored light evokes tactile sensation, manifesting as perceived temperature.
findings.quote: colored light may evoke a tactile sensation in the perceiver (according to the range of chromatic hue), manifesting itself in the form of perceived temperature

findings.consequent: Brainwork for reconstruction/classification of reality, syntax rules of visual perception
findings.mechanism: Light supports the brainwork for reconstruction and classification of reality, setting visual perception rules.
findings.quote: light is, therefore, a device (natural or artificial) that supports the brainworkofreconstruction and classification of reality by the viewer, setting the syntax rules of visual perception

findings.consequent: Meaning to environment, interpretation of reality, adaptation to reality, control of external environment (in cognitive uncertainty)
findings.mechanism: Light helps give meaning to the environment and drives interpretation/adaptation processes, especially in cognitive uncertainty.
findings.quote: light helps to give meaning to the environment and drive the process of interpretation of reality (but also adaptation to that), performed by a subject in a state of cognitive uncertainty

findings.consequent: Attraction, involvement, stimulation, fascination (due to mystery/complexity)
findings.mechanism: Light's shades and gradations attract, involve, stimulate, and fascinate due to perceived mystery and complexity.
findings.quote: light, with its many shades and gradations, leads the individual through the process of exploration towards the unknown: paradoxically, light seems to hide, rather than reveal the mystery, but just for this it attracts, involves, stimulates and fascinates us so much.

findings.consequent: Specific emotions, behaviors, mood, bodily/mental health, aesthetic appreciation
findings.mechanism: Light stimuli induce specific emotions, behaviors, mood, influence bodily/mental health, and aesthetic appreciation.
findings.quote: light stimuli (i.e. sensory input) will be able to induce specific emotions, behaviours and mood (Fusco, 2005b, 2012; Fusco et al., 2011; Tomassoni, 2014), as well as influence bodily and mental health, but also the level of aesthetic appreciation

findings.antecedent: Light (natural or artificial, colored or fluorescent, evanescent or material)
findings.consequent: Perceptive alterations within human sensory sphere, effectiveness of lit environment
findings.mechanism: Light's capacity to induce perceptive alterations is key to the effectiveness of any lit environment.
findings.quote: Due to the capacity of light—whether natural or artificial, colored or fluorescent, evanescent or material—to induce specific perceptive alterations within the sensory sphere of the human, the holistic, all-encompassing, and immersive dimension of individual involvement is, therefore, the key to the effectiveness of any lit environment.

findings.antecedent: Object location + light sources (angle of incidence) + object capacity (absorbing/reflecting light)
findings.consequent: Human perception, emotions, bodily/mental wellness
findings.mechanism: Object location and light interaction (absorption/reflection) drive human perception, emotions, and wellness.
findings.quote: the location of an object within the environment, according to the angle of incidence of one or more light sources, as well as the capacity of the object in absorbing and reflecting the light (luminous radiance or reflectance), are capable of driving human perception and emotions, as well as influencing the bodily and mental wellness

findings.antecedent: Light Design (cumulative effect of object + light + environment)
findings.consequent: Specific emotions, behaviors, psychophysical feedbacks, health, wellness
findings.mechanism: Light Design induces specific emotions, behaviors, and psychophysical feedbacks, influencing health and wellness.
findings.quote: Light Design takes advantage of that cumulative effect, related to the sum of all the above factors (object + light + environment) to induce specific emotions, behaviours and psychophysical feedbacks by the perceiver, influencing his/her health and wellness.

findings.antecedent: Light Art (various light sources, mixed with items, exhibition strategy)
findings.consequent: Different emotions, behaviors, aesthetic appreciation
findings.mechanism: Light Art excites different emotions and behaviors during aesthetic appreciation.
findings.quote: The so-called Light Art, for example, uses various types light sources... to produce an overall perceptual effect in the perceiver, exciting different emotions and behaviours during the individual experience of aesthetic appreciation.

findings.antecedent: Dark (absence of light), different light intensities (overlaps, intersections)
findings.consequent: Environmental organization, shadows, depth, modulated feelings and emotions
findings.mechanism: Dark and light intensity variations contribute to environmental organization, creating shadows/depth and modulating feelings/emotions.
findings.quote: Even the dark, namely absence of light, contributes to organize and set out the surrounding environment... overlaps and intersections generated by different light intensities, are able to create shadows and depth, modulating feelings and emotions

findings.consequent: Color perception, mood, behavior
findings.mechanism: Light determines color perception, influencing mood and behavior.
findings.quote: light determines the colour perception of the objects inside a lit environment, influencing the mood and behaviour of people exposed

findings.consequent: Neuropsychiatric effects
findings.mechanism: Sensory deprivation, especially light deprivation, has negative neuropsychiatric effects.
findings.quote: The "Sendep" (i.e. sensory deprivation) or perceptual isolation, especially about light, has negative effects on the human being from a neuropsychiatric perspective

findings.antecedent: Constant and uniform light stimulus (Ganzfeld Effect)
findings.consequent: Sensory deprivation-like effects, disorientation, 'fullness of emptiness', horizon's absence, altered perception of real space
findings.mechanism: The Ganzfeld Effect (constant, uniform light) leads to sensory deprivation-like effects, disorientation, and altered perception.
findings.quote: A related phenomenon is the so-called Ganzfeld Effect (or perceptual deprivation), that occurs when a constant and uniform light stimulus is used... this leads to effects similar to sensory deprivation

findings.consequent: Biochemical/hormonal processes, body temperature, mood, psychological well-being, electrical brain activity, neurotransmitters
findings.mechanism: Light influences biochemical/hormonal processes, body temperature, mood, psychological well-being, electrical brain activity, and neurotransmitters.
findings.quote: light influences biochemical and hormonal processes, body temperature, mood, psychological well-being and electrical brain activity, influencing the neurotransmitters

findings.antecedent: Low lighting + warm colours / pastel shades (in public spaces)
findings.consequent: Relaxation, sense of protection, hospitality
findings.mechanism: Low lighting with warm colors/pastel shades induces relaxation, protection, and hospitality in public spaces.
findings.quote: low lighting is used, accompanied by warm colours or pastel shades, in order to induce relaxation and evoke a sense of protection and hospitality

findings.antecedent: High lighting + colder chromatic temperatures (in production/competitive environments)
findings.consequent: Work efficiency, productivity, aggressiveness, competition
findings.mechanism: High lighting with colder chromatic temperatures stimulates work efficiency, productivity, aggressiveness, and competition.
findings.quote: high lighting accompanied by colder chromatic temperatures is able to stimulate a greater work efficiency and productivity, but also aggressiveness and competition

findings.antecedent: Bioelectric signals transmitted to the brain by photoreceptors (scanning light photons)
findings.consequent: Aesthetic quality of reality, correlation between perceptual processes and visual brain
findings.mechanism: Bioelectric signals from photoreceptors determine aesthetic quality and correlate with perceptual processes and the visual brain.
findings.quote: the functional specialization of cerebral cortex has showed that the bioelectric signals transmitted to the brain by the photoreceptors, namely neurons specialized in scanning the light photons, determine the aesthetic quality of the reality perceived by humans, demonstrating the correlation between perceptual processes and vis-ual brain

findings.antecedent: Light intercepted and reflected by an object
findings.consequent: Perception of spatial relationships
findings.mechanism: Viewers perceive spatial relationships only when light is intercepted and reflected by an object.
findings.quote: viewers perceive spatial relationships only when light is intercepted and reflected by an object settled in a space-light context

findings.consequent: Higher level of concentration/attention, greater emotional response
findings.mechanism: Higher intensity of light stimulation increases concentration/attention and emotional response.
findings.quote: generally, a higher intensity of light sti-mulation corresponds to a higher level of concentration/attention, associated with a greater emotional response by the subject.

findings.antecedent: Flashing or pulsating light (vs. steady light)
findings.consequent: Faster emotional responses, innate state of alert, influenced judgment abilities, problem solving, decision making skills
findings.mechanism: Flashing/pulsating light induces faster emotional responses, activates an alert state, and influences cognitive skills.
findings.quote: flashing or pulsating light (rather than a steady light) induces faster emotional responses by the perceiver: in fact, flashing light is associated with the danger, activating an innate state of alert in the human, enabling him/her to react quickly and in a most extreme way, influencing judgment abilities, problem solving and decision making skills.

findings.consequent: Different emotions (physical attraction, aggressiveness)
findings.mechanism: Lighting modulation and color spectrum stimulate different emotions.
findings.quote: Through the lighting modulation (and its colour spectrum), it is possible to stimulate different emotions in human being, such as physical attraction or aggres-siveness

findings.consequent: Activation of specific neurotransmitters, production of specific hormones, psychobiological bases of light perception (changing according to sex/age)
findings.mechanism: Colored light activates neurotransmitters and produces hormones, influencing light perception based on sex/age.
findings.quote: the activation of specific neurotransmitters and the production, at biochemical level, of specific hor-mones in the presence of determined colour light source, shows the psychobiological bases of light perception by human, that may change according to the subject's sex or age

findings.antecedent: Lighting conditions, intensity, colour of light source
findings.consequent: Human biological cycles, circadian rhythm, level of hormonal secretions (melatonin)
findings.mechanism: Lighting conditions, intensity, and color influence biological cycles and circadian rhythm by affecting melatonin levels.
findings.quote: Lighting conditions, as well as the intensity and colour of the light source, influence indeed the human bio-logical cycles and, by a chronopsychological point of view, the circadian rhythm, by increasing or decreasing the level of specific hormonal secretions (such as melatonin, namely the marker-hormone of circadian rhythms, produced by the pineal gland), that are responsible for certain neurophysiological states.

findings.consequent: Melatonin production, concentration
findings.mechanism: Higher/lower lighting levels inhibit melatonin production, inducing higher concentration.
findings.quote: throughthe use of higher or lower lighting levels, it is possible to inhibit the production of melatonin, inducing a higher concentration

findings.consequent: Melatonin levels, sleep onset
findings.mechanism: Low light increases melatonin levels and stimulates sleep onset.
findings.quote: melatonin levels increase during the night, when light is low, stimulating the sleep onset

findings.consequent: Dazzle, reduced visibility, reduced visual performance, discomfort, stress, sense of danger, disorientation, neuropsychiatric disorders (if sustained)
findings.mechanism: Over-lighting/flashes cause dazzle, reduced visibility/performance, discomfort, stress, danger, disorientation, and potential neuropsychiatric disorders.
findings.quote: over-lighting or close light flashes provoke dazzle, that by reducing the perceiver's visi-bility and visual performance, bring out discomfort, stress, sense of danger, and disorientation in the individual, that if sustained over time may lead to neuropsychiatric disorders

stimuli.description: General light stimulus, dark/lighting deprivation, light type/range/colors, strategic lighting layout/modulation, light intensity/saturation/modulation, sound stream, colored light (chromatic hue), natural/artificial light, object location/light interaction, Light Design, Light Art, constant/uniform light, low/high lighting levels, warm/cold chromatic temperatures, flashing/pulsating light
